blogs.title: Rule 404(b) and the “Intrinsic” Firearm Evidence Test: Why the Eighth Circuit’s Decision Matters
blogs.description: This post dissects the court’s treatment of the sawed‑off Marlin .22 as intrinsic evidence, exploring the precedent of United States v. Battle and the continuing debate over whether prior possession should be admissible to prove later control or ownership. It examines the subtle line between relevant and propitious evidence, and what this ruling signals for criminal trials that hinge on weapon possession testimonies.

blogs.title: The 3553(a) Post‑Guideline Sentencing Debate: How the Eighth Circuit Reinforces the “Sufficient but Not Greater Than Necessary” Doctrine
blogs.description: Focusing on the sentencing portion of the opinion, this article analyzes how the court applied the USSG § 2K2.1(b)(6)(B) enhancement and the 3553(a) factors to justify a 292‑month sentence. It highlights the court’s reliance on precedent such as Gall, Goodhouse, and Masood, and discusses the broader trend toward deference in post‑guideline sentencing disputes and the limits of appellate review.

blogs.title: A Inside Look at Evidentiary Abuses: Confrontation, Hearsay, and Striking Testimony in Federal Trials
blogs.description: This piece reviews the court’s rulings on DF’s statements to police, her testimony about her sister’s death, and the government’s control over external police reports. It examines the interplay of the Confrontation Clause, Rule 403 prejudice, and the court’s obligation to provide limiting instructions, offering practitioners a guide to navigating similar evidentiary maze in federal criminal prosecutions.

blogs.title: United States v. Cutbank: The Practical Implications of the Armed Career Criminal Act’s Felon‑in‑Possession Enhancements
blogs.description: This blog breaks down the PCIA enhancement calculations in the case, comparing the PSR-derived offense level against the Armed Career Criminal Act toxicity. It evaluates how the court's application of the four‑level 2K2.1(b)(6)(B) enhancement fit within the broader context of statutory interpretation of “use or possession in connection with another felony” and what it means for future Armed Career Criminal Act cases.
